title: IAQ exceedance classification from low-cost ambient sensors: code, configuration and results for a leakage-aware benchmark
description: Code, configuration file (config.yaml), selected hyperparameters and thresholds for every fold, per-day and per-home metrics, and all out-of-sample predictions for a leakage-aware evaluation of twelve machine learning classifiers and simple rules (light, relative-humidity, sound-level and working-hours thresholds) that flag indoor air quality exceedances from temperature, relative humidity and light or sound signals. Study 1: CO2 > 1000 ppm (ICOP-IAQ 2010) in an office room (Occupancy Detection dataset, Candanedo & Feldheim, 2016). Study 2: CO2, PM2.5 or TVOC exceedances in 95 home offices (Manu & Rysanek, 2024). Validation: random, leave-one-day-out, leave-sites-out, chronological, buffered leave-one-day-out, forward-chaining and unseen-homes-future-period protocols, with alarm-burden and episode analyses. Supplementary analysis: DALTON (Karmakar et al., 2024; rebuilt by scripts) and Lovric et al. (2025). One command (run_all.sh) regenerates every table and figure. Source: https://github.com/hamirulhamizan/iaq-lowcost-sensing-benchmark
